A NAMED SUBSTRATE DEFECT IN THE BRIEF IS ALREADY SOLVED ON DISK. The brief records 'rules/ live-vs-repo drift is TWO-DIRECTIONAL (5/88 identical); no safe sync direction exists yet.' tools/harness-drift is exactly the deterministic two-directional differ for that question: it normalises line endings first (so a CRLF working tree vs an LF blob does not manufacture phantom diffs), runs difflib.SequenceMatcher on every non-identical pair, records BOTH only_repo and only_live counts, requires only_live==0 for REPO-AHEAD and only_repo==0 for LIVE-AHEAD, and errs toward DIVERGED. The prior archaeology pass marked it UNKNOWN-NEEDS-PROBE solely because it has no README. Its docstring cites the measurement that justifies it: an LLM fan-out over the same 338 files scored 86% with 100% of errors in the DANGEROUS direction (31 files called deploy-safe that were two-way DIVERGED).

COMPOSE candidate: workflows/rtv-pdr.js explicitly instructs that it be gated behind tools/ese-gate ('Gate this workflow behind the ESE (Ensemble Semantic Entropy) escalation gate - fire only on hard/contentious work-units'), because it costs N parallel Opus rollouts per invocation. ESE decides cheaply (deterministic, threshold 0.5, fail-toward-escalation on every degenerate input); rtv-pdr pays only when the unit is contentious. Two already-built halves of one mechanism.

MECHANICAL-GATE-BEFORE-LLM is the cheapest high-value pattern in the range and is already implemented twice: plan-gate runs a ~1 ms python stage-0 lint before N Opus reviewers, and tools/mcpctl asserts read-only-BY-CONSTRUCTION over the AST of every module rather than trusting a sentence. Both are directly applicable to a 2,007-unit run (pre-filter units mechanically; enforce read-only agent scope mechanically instead of by prompt).
